chunks: Ali ibn al-Hasan from his two brothers from their father from Muhammad ibn Abdillah from Abdillah ibn Bukayr from Muhammad ibn Muslim and Abu Basir, who said:
Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'There is no khula' (divorce by redemption) except during a period of purity (from menstruation) in which there has been no sexual intercourse.'

key_terms.الطُّهْرُ: Purity: A state free from major impurity, specifically referring here to the period between menstrual cycles.
key_terms.الْجِمَاعُ: Intercourse: Sexual intercourse, the occurrence of which affects the validity of the purity period for this ruling.
key_terms.الْخُلْعُ: Khula: Divorce initiated by the wife, typically involving financial compensation to the husband.

ai.seo_question: What is the condition of purity required for a valid Khula divorce in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the juristic condition of *tuhr* (ritual purity) for the validity of *khula*, specifying that the period must be free from both menstruation and prior sexual intercourse within that cycle. This distinction is crucial in Shia fiqh to ensure the woman is in a state of complete purity, distinguishing it from the general *iddah* requirements for *talaq*. It underscores the precision with which the Imams delineated the procedural validity of marital dissolution mechanisms.
